description: What one unit of one piecework activity is worth at one company, from one date. The rate table a Farm Salary Structure inherits from when it names no rate of its own: payroll reads the structure's base_rate first, because a negotiated rate is the more specific record, and falls back to the active row here for the employee's company and activity. One row per (company, activity, effective_from) — raising next season's rate is a new row with a new effective_from, not an edit to the one that paid last season.

fields.description: Which piecework this rate pays for — the same vocabulary ML Model.piecework_activity uses, e.g. 'bucket_segmentation'. Matched case-insensitively against the activity a salary structure names, so 'Bucket Segmentation' and 'bucket_segmentation' are the same activity.
fields.label: Activity

fields.description: What one unit is paid — one bucket, one bin, one tree.
fields.label: Rate Per Unit

fields.description: The kill switch. An inactive row is never read by payroll, whatever its dates say.
fields.label: Active

fields.description: Leave blank for the rate in force now. Where two rows both cover a date, the later effective_from wins.
fields.label: Effective To

fields.description: What this rate is for, in the words somebody setting it would use — 'Cherry picking, 2026 season'.
fields.label: Description

name: Piecework Rate
